correctness.rationale: The Legendre antiderivative identity produces the exact quadratic step-derivative kernel. BV functions decompose into signed measures of jumps, so the sharp norm is the maximum L1 kernel variation. A central jump gives 15 sqrt(21)/28-5/8. Near-center global dominance is established by eight positive rational Bernstein coefficients on the entire square-parameter interval. The remaining continuum is covered by 300 exact root-bracket integrations plus an analytical 75/2 derivative bound. The standalone Python standard-library checker verifies all polynomial identities, exact rational inequalities, and covering intervals.

value.rationale: This resolves the exact operator-stability invariant for the first degree of Legendre truncation whose jump derivative is genuinely quadratic, proving a midpoint extremizer and sharp 82.995% variation amplification. This has direct relevance to edge stability of low-order spectral approximation, and it is neither a bare coefficient calculation for a chosen input nor a consequence of the nearby quadratic result: global sharpness requires a substantial continuum parameter optimization with a reproducible rational certificate.
